blocks.text: empower inspectors and project managers to streamline on-site construction inspections by overlaying dynamic checklists, contextual data, and real-time collaboration tools through AR glasses, while reducing costs and ensuring compliance?

items: Streamline inspection flows
Improve data and accuracy
Reduce costs and increase efficiency
Enhance collaboration and compliance
Future-proof AI + AR
Conducted competitive audits of existing construction inspection apps and AR-enabled field tools.
Interviewed inspectors, project managers, and engineers across trades to uncover pain points in workflows, checklists, and reporting.
Identified high-need use cases: role-specific inspection checklists, before/after comparisons, and cost verification workflows.
Reviewed academic and industry sources on AR in construction, wearable-assisted inspections, and spatial computing.
Explored challenges in data compliance, law/recall notifications, and construction order finalization.
Identified trust, accuracy, and real-time collaboration as essential UX considerations, beyond hardware specs.
Used findings to inform principles for checklist design, visual layering, and mobile–AR integration.

blocks.text: Conducted interviews to gather insights from users and stakeholders (implied by mention of stakeholder interviews).

items: Used insights to shape inspection templates, room-based checklists, and tailored dashboards.
Captured requirements for role-specific “ingredient lists” (e.g., scanner, notes, tape measure).
Helped refine the goals of cost reduction, accuracy, and real-time updates across multiple contractors.

blocks.text: Tested prototypes with users to assess emotional support, clarity, and personalization.

items: Gathered feedback on AR checklist readability, voice/gesture commands, and navigation triggers.
Measured efficiency: time saved compared to manual inspections and paper-based workflows.
Used findings to refine visual hierarchy, session summaries, and integration with maps + reminders.
Developed low- and high-fidelity prototypes for mobile and AR glasses.
Designed a modular UI system for uploading inspection checklists, attaching before/after photos, and role-based task lists.
Prototyped AR overlays including:Room-wise task listsVideo-assisted inspection referencesLaw/recall notificationsCost/order verification prompts
Created interactive flows simulating site inspections with Even Realities G1 glasses.
Iterated prototypes with stakeholders for validation and alignment with real-world workflows.
Dashboard Banner: Displays AR-driven task information (to-do list, floor plan, live inspection data).
AI Status Module (Omni-AI, Excellent): Real-time system feedback on inspection/AI status.
Active Apps Section: Toggle control for apps in use (To-Do List, Map).
Inactive Apps Section: Secondary options (Translate, Camera) to activate as needed.
Suggested Apps: Personalized extension discovery with one-tap install (App Store style).
Top Navigation: User/account access via profile + notifications.

controls.heading: Productivity First
controls.bodyText: Prioritizes utility and tools, not just media.

controls.heading: Modular + Flexible
controls.bodyText: Clear segmentation between active, inactive, and suggested apps makes system extensible.

controls.heading: Mobile–AR Bridge:
controls.bodyText: Designed to mirror AR glasses UI (simple toggles, spatial task context).

controls.heading: Trust-building
controls.bodyText: Omni-AI status builds confidence by surfacing clarity (“Excellent”) upfront.

items: Content-centric: Prioritizes large thumbnails so users can browse visually, reducing cognitive load.
Simplicity + Familiarity: Mirrors social apps (Instagram Explore, YouTube library), making it intuitive.
Scalable: Grid layout supports expansion to more media types (photos, 360 images, AR models).
Contribution-first: The purple upload CTA signals active participation, not just passive browsing.

controls.heading: Upload Media Button
controls.bodyText: Prominent call-to-action in the center, encouraging contribution.

controls.heading: Popular Content Grid
controls.bodyText: Visual-first layout with thumbnails, titles, and quick delete (X) actions.
